blocks.text: Quick verdict

ProxyEmpire is the better value for most buyers in 2026. Its residential traffic currently starts at $3.50/GB against IPRoyal's $7 for a single gigabyte, ISP-level targeting is included free, and its $1.97 trial covers both residential and mobile. IPRoyal wins when you need very long sticky sessions (up to seven days, against ProxyEmpire's 24 hours), when you want ISP, datacenter and a request-billed Web Unblocker in the same account, or when you would rather trust a provider with more independent benchmark history. Both let unused traffic carry forward, so neither punishes irregular usage.

IPRoyal and ProxyEmpire are often shortlisted together for one reason: both let you keep the residential traffic you pay for instead of losing it at the end of the month. That makes this comparison less about who rolls over bandwidth and more about price per gigabyte, session length, targeting depth and the extras each one bundles. If your workload is irregular and you hate paying for unused gigabytes, these are two of the best-suited providers on the market, and the differences between them are worth understanding.

blocks.text: IPRoyal in 2026: what you get

IPRoyal is a value-focused provider best known for residential traffic that never expires. You can buy a single gigabyte, use it over months, and top up when you need to, which suits irregular projects better than monthly allowances. The residential pool is advertised at 32M+ IPs across 195 countries with state and city targeting, and sticky sessions can be requested for up to seven days. IPRoyal also sells ISP, datacenter and mobile proxies and a Web Unblocker billed per successful request.

Strengths: Residential traffic that does not expire; Sticky sessions up to 7 days; Can start with a single gigabyte; Several proxy types plus Web Unblocker in one account. Weak spots: Smaller pool than the enterprise networks; Headline $1.75/GB rate needs a 10 TB purchase; Mid-volume prices are not published.
ProxyEmpire in 2026: what you get

ProxyEmpire sells residential, mobile, static residential and datacenter proxies from one dashboard and competes on flexibility. Traffic you prepay never expires, ISP-level targeting is free, and the $1.97 trial lets you test both residential and mobile networks before committing. Its 30M+ advertised pool is smaller on paper than the enterprise providers, but independent testing has rated its real reachable pool well relative to its claims.

Strengths: Prepaid traffic rolls over indefinitely; ISP/ASN targeting included at no extra cost; Cheap $1.97 trial covering residential and mobile; Unlimited residential option priced per day. Weak spots: Smaller advertised pool than the big three; Exact GB thresholds for each tier only shown at checkout; Weaker results on Google in some independent tests.
Pricing: IPRoyal vs ProxyEmpire

IPRoyal's residential subscription costs $7 for 1 GB, $11.90 for 2 GB and $52.50 for 10 GB ($5.25/GB); pay-as-you-go is 5% more ($7.35 for 1 GB). The advertised $1.75/GB rate applies only at 10 TB. Prices for custom volumes such as 25, 100 or 500 GB are calculated in the dashboard.

ProxyEmpire's rotating residential pricing currently starts at $3.50/GB (shown as 50% off a $7 list price) and steps down through several tiers to $1.50/GB at 1 TB, with custom pricing from about $0.75/GB above 5 TB. Rotating mobile starts at $4.50/GB, rotating datacenter at about $0.65/GB, and a flat-rate unlimited residential plan is sold by the day.

Buying 10 GB, you would pay about $35 with ProxyEmpire and $52.50 with IPRoyal: a 33% saving in ProxyEmpire's favour. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because IPRoyal and ProxyEmpire do not publish an exact price for that volume. Neither provider makes you use it or lose it: both IPRoyal and ProxyEmpire let unused traffic carry forward, so the comparison really comes down to rate and features.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

On paper the two networks are similar in size: IPRoyal advertises 32M+ residential IPs and ProxyEmpire advertises 30M+. Advertised pool sizes are marketing figures counted over long periods; the number of IPs actually reachable in a given country at a given moment is far smaller for every provider, so treat these as a rough guide to depth rather than a guarantee. For coverage, IPRoyal lists 195 countries and ProxyEmpire lists 170+. On targeting, IPRoyal offers country, state and city (ISP selection needs verification), while ProxyEmpire offers country, region, city and ISP/ASN (included by default).
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, IPRoyal offers rotating or sticky sessions from 1 second up to 7 days, and ProxyEmpire offers rotating or sticky sessions up to 24 hours. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With IPRoyal: solid success rates and non-expiring traffic for bursty crawls. With ProxyEmpire: stable connections and traffic that never expires. Run the same small test on both before committing.

SERP and rank tracking: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. IPRoyal: it works, but it has no dedicated SERP product. ProxyEmpire: Google was its weakest target in independent tests. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Social media and multi-account management: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: 7-day sticky sessions keep one IP on one account. How ProxyEmpire compares: residential and mobile IPs with 24-hour sticky sessions.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With IPRoyal: city targeting with pay-only-for-what-you-use traffic. With ProxyEmpire: free city and ISP targeting. Run the same small test on both before committing.

Ad verification and geo-testing: ProxyEmpire. ProxyEmpire has the edge here. Why: ISP-level targeting at no extra cost. How IPRoyal compares: decent coverage but no ASN or carrier targeting on standard accounts.

Tight budgets: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With IPRoyal: small entry purchases and traffic that never expires. With ProxyEmpire: rollover means nothing you pay for is wasted. Run the same small test on both before committing.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. IPRoyal: No general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies. ProxyEmpire: $1.97 trial with 100 MB residential and 50 MB mobile. Verification and payment rules differ too. IPRoyal: Optional ID verification; required for ISP-level targeting and PayPal. ProxyEmpire: Standard verification. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test IPRoyal and ProxyEmpire before you commit
The quickest way to choose between IPRoyal and ProxyEmpire is a side-by-side test on the sites and countries you actually care about:

1. Buy the smallest option on each side (IPRoyal: no general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies; ProxyEmpire: $1.97 trial with 100 MB residential and 50 MB mobile). 2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, IPRoyal comes out ahead in 1, ProxyEmpire in 1, and 4 are ties. With no overall winner, decide on the factor that matters most to you: IPRoyal is strongest for irregular or seasonal projects, while ProxyEmpire is strongest for teams that hate losing unused bandwidth. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
